rows.note: This is the all-purpose spoken choice when someone is forced or pressured to do something.

example.english: My boss used pressure to oblige me to work late today.
example.traditional: 老闆逼我今日返工返到好夜。
example.jyutping: lou5 baan2 bik1 ngo5 gam1 jat6 faan1 gung1 faan1 dou3 hou2 je6

rows.note: Use this when obliging someone means helping them or doing them a favour.

example.english: I came over to help you move on moving day—I was happy to oblige.
example.traditional: 你搬屋嗰日，我過嚟幫手，唔使客氣。
example.jyutping: nei5 bun1 uk1 go2 jat6 ngo5 gwo3 lai4 bong1 sau2 m4 sai2 haak3 hei3

rows.note: Use this when acknowledging that someone’s help has put you in their debt and expressing sincere gratitude.

example.english: You found me a job this time, so I’m truly in your debt; I hope to oblige you in return.
example.traditional: 今次多得你幫我搵到份工，真係承你情。
example.jyutping: gam1 ci3 do1 dak1 nei5 bong1 ngo5 wan2 dou3 fan6 gung1 zan1 hai6 sing4 nei5 cing4
